summary: Modules should start with #!/usr/bin/python (or the right interpreter) so ansible_python_interpreter works; avoid #!/usr/bin/env and interpreter arguments, binaries need no shebang, and encoding comments are unnecessary since ansible-core 2.17.
questions: What shebang should my Ansible module use?
Why shouldn't I use #!/usr/bin/env python in a module?
Do I still need a coding: utf-8 comment in modules?
Do binary modules need a shebang?

answer_card.title: Module shebang
answer_card.answer_md:
- Start with `#!/usr/bin/python` so `ansible_python_interpreter` works (or `#!/usr/bin/<interp>` for other languages).
- **Don't** use `#!/usr/bin/env`; it bypasses interpreter logic. Shebang arguments don't work.
- Binary modules need no shebang.
- Drop `# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-`; unnecessary since ansible-core 2.17 dropped Python 2.
